cells.tense: The practice is running clean right now, and the direction you've chosen is holding.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Choose something you already handle well and examine only the detail you normally pass over. Stay there longer than feels finished, then set it down — not when it starts to hurt.
cells.core:
You're in the stretch where the work is deepening, and the deepening isn't costing you much. That's the sign it's real: the hours go in, the direction holds, and you come back to the bench without having to talk yourself into it. Nothing here needs fixing.

What this balance wants to feed is a sharper distinction, not more hours. Choose something you already handle well and go a single layer deeper. Not the whole craft — one detail, studied until you can say plainly why it's done this way and not the other. The refining is the point, not the finished thing. When you're done, let it rest for today and shut the book. That's what keeps practice from turning into pressure.
cells.sheetLine: The work is deepening because you keep showing up to it.
cells.verb: staying at the work until the work gets deep
cells.place: the stretch of road where your effort is aimed at what's ahead

cells.tense: You're already at next month's version of the work while today's is still on the bench.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, out loud
cells.ask: When a piece of what you're building comes out right, tell the people near you that it came out right, out loud, before you move to the next stage.
cells.core:
The direction is real, but the pace has run past the thing it's carrying. You can see the next three stages from here, so you're already living in them — and the current one, the one that actually needs your hands, keeps getting skipped. From the outside it looks like nothing is ever allowed to land. You're not behind. You're out front, which is its own way of not being here.

What's thin is the moment when a good thing gets marked with other people. Not a ceremony, just saying it while it's still warm: this part came out right. That's what breaks the forward lean. The people who share your days are part of the work whether or not they're on the crew — let them hear one thing finish before you've moved on. The build will still be there after.
cells.sheetLine: You're on the next stage while this one's still drying.

cells.tense: There's a door you already walked through and you're still standing outside it.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: Say once, plainly, to whoever it concerns, the outline of what you're building and what it asks of them. No pitch for it — just the outline.
cells.core:
Whatever used to carry the work forward has gone quiet. Not lost, just not moving — the direction is still there, but you've stopped putting weight behind it, and the work has stopped asking. This isn't a failure of will. It's what happens when effort gets pulled back long enough that the pulling back becomes the habit.

Here's what moves it: declare the shape of it, outward, once. Not a pitch and not an apology — the plain outline of what you're building and what it needs from others. Saying it before anyone asks does something the private version can't: it puts the thing somewhere it can be answered. One sentence, no rehearsal. The energy comes back through the saying, not before it.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the shape of it and you've stopped saying it.

cells.tense: The work you call yours is being built right now, by you, on a schedule you didn't set.
cells.act: do the next piece at the speed you can keep for a month, not the speed you can keep for a day
cells.ask: Tomorrow, take the next piece of work at the pace you could hold for a month. Same task, slower — and notice whether the slower pace feels wrong.
cells.core:
There's momentum in your days that you'd say isn't yours — the work is getting done, but the account you give of it is that something else is driving. You'd tell anyone you're just keeping up. That pace is authored, and the author hasn't signed it.

Nothing needs taking apart. The move is to slow one piece down to a human speed and feel what the speed was doing. Tomorrow, take the next unit of work at the pace you could actually keep for a month — not the surge you keep for a day. Same task, less velocity. Then check the one thing that tells you who's steering: does the slower pace feel wrong because someone is waiting on you, or because you don't believe in the work at that speed? The answer is usually in the second one, and it's yours to look at.
cells.sheetLine: Something keeps the work moving, and you don't sign for it.
cells.verb: staying at the work until the work gets deep
cells.place: the stretch of road where your effort is aimed at what's ahead

attempts.check: The record supports sustained craft reaching a threshold of real skill, but not that the person's practice is actually at that threshold, so 'the work is deepening past where you can see it' is my extrapolation from the draw. A reader could reasonably say the craft is early or the direction is borrowed rather than their own. The asks survive being wrong because each is one bounded act with no promised outcome. The sentence that serves me more than them: 'each pass goes deeper than the last' — it flatters the mechanism; I cut it.
